name: Rehum
overview: Rehum was a male figure who returned to Judah following the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah. He is noted in Scripture under two names, Rehum and Nehum, reflecting a connection to the post-exilic community restoration. No specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Rehum means '[he] is compassionate,' while the alternate name Nehum means 'comfort.' Both names suggest qualities of mercy and consolation, which may reflect the character or role of this individual during the return to Judah. These names are proper names not indicated as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Rehum as a descendant of Jacob, which places him within the broader covenant community of Israel. Beyond this inferred lineage, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Rehum's significance lies in his participation in the return from Babylonian exile, marking him as part of the faithful remnant who restored the worship and community life in Judah. His mention in both Ezra and Nehemiah highlights his role in the foundational period of Israel's post-exilic restoration. The dual naming underscores the continuity and encouragement present in this era of renewal.
